summary: The original research code for 3D Gaussian Splatting: turn a set of photos into a 3D scene you can view in real time.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: This is the reference implementation of the paper 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering from Inria. It trains a 3D model made of many small Gaussians from photos of a scene (via COLMAP structure-from-motion data), then renders new views in real time. The codebase has four parts: a PyTorch optimizer that trains models, a network viewer to watch training, an OpenGL real-time viewer, and a script that turns your own images into a training-ready dataset.
sixtySeconds.problem: Earlier neural rendering methods were slow to train and render. Gaussian Splatting gives high-quality novel views at real-time speed.
whoFor: 3D capture enthusiasts with a strong GPU
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Use it to reproduce the original method or train scenes from your own photos with the authors' code.
requirements: 24 GB VRAM to train at paper quality (the FAQ covers smaller setups)
Conda, a C++ compiler and CUDA SDK 11 (11.8 was used)

overview: Clone with --recursive, then create the Conda environment from environment.yml and activate gaussian_splatting. It assumes CUDA SDK 11, not 12.
Train with python train.py -s pointing at a COLMAP or NeRF Synthetic dataset; use convert.py to prepare your own images.
View results with the SIBR viewers; pre-built Windows binaries are offered. Tested on Windows 10 and Ubuntu 22.04. The license allows research use only.
limitations: Building viewers and submodules can be tricky, especially on Windows

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.body: On Windows, first run SET DISTUTILS_USE_SDK=1.

steps.title: Get pre-built viewers
steps.body: Download the pre-built SIBR viewer binaries for Windows linked in the README, which the authors recommend over building.

firstRun.title: Train on a sample scene
firstRun.body: Download the T&T+DB COLMAP dataset linked in the README and train on one scene.

tutorial.title: Train and view a scene
tutorial.useCase: The README's training and viewer commands.
setup: A COLMAP or NeRF Synthetic dataset

steps.title: Train
steps.code: python train.py -s <path to COLMAP or NeRF Synthetic dataset>

steps.title: Render and score (optional)
steps.body: python render.py -m <path to trained model> then python metrics.py -m <path to trained model>.

tutorial.expected: A trained Gaussian scene you can fly through in the viewer.
